I have the prescription frequencies. Now let me compute the 7-day treatment-change rate — defined as a switch to a *different* antimicrobial class within 7 days of a given class's exposure. Let me build this per class, keeping the query bounded.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH abx AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, de.drug_exposure_start_date AS dt, anc.concept_code AS atc, anc.concept_name AS class_name
  FROM omop.concept anc
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.ancestor_concept_id = anc.concept_id
  JOIN omop.drug_exposure de ON de.drug_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  WHERE anc.vocabulary_id='ATC' AND anc.concept_class_id='ATC 3rd'
    AND anc.concept_code IN ('J01C','J01D','J01F','J01M','J01E','J01X','J01A','J01G')
),
idx AS (
  SELECT person_id, atc, class_name, dt,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY person_id, atc ORDER BY dt) AS rn
  FROM abx
)
SELECT i.class_name, i.atc,
       COUNT(*) AS n_index_starts,
       SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM abx b
             WHERE b.person_id=i.person_id AND b.atc<>i.atc
               AND b.dt > i.dt AND b.dt <= i.dt + 7
           ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_switch_7d
FROM idx i
WHERE i.rn=1
GROUP BY i.class_name, i.atc
ORDER BY n_index_starts DESC;

arguments.sql_query:
WITH abx AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, de.drug_exposure_start_date AS dt, anc.concept_code AS atc, anc.concept_name AS class_name
  FROM omop.concept anc
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.ancestor_concept_id = anc.concept_id
  JOIN omop.drug_exposure de ON de.drug_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  WHERE anc.vocabulary_id='ATC' AND anc.concept_class_id='ATC 3rd'
    AND anc.concept_code IN ('J01C','J01D','J01F','J01M','J01E','J01X','J01A','J01G')
),
idx AS (
  SELECT person_id, atc, class_name, dt,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY person_id, atc ORDER BY dt) AS rn
  FROM abx
),
idx1 AS (SELECT * FROM idx WHERE rn=1),
flagged AS (
  SELECT i.class_name, i.atc, i.person_id, i.dt,
         MAX(CASE WHEN b.person_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS switched
  FROM idx1 i
  LEFT JOIN abx b
    ON b.person_id=i.person_id AND b.atc<>i.atc
   AND b.dt > i.dt AND b.dt <= DATEADD(day,7,i.dt)
  GROUP BY i.class_name, i.atc, i.person_id, i.dt
)
SELECT class_name, atc,
       COUNT(*) AS n_index_starts,
       SUM(switched) AS n_switch_7d,
       CAST(100.0*SUM(switched)/COUNT(*) AS DECIMAL(5,1)) AS pct_switch_7d
FROM flagged
GROUP BY class_name, atc
ORDER BY n_index_starts DESC;

## What the local EHR shows (OMOP, ATC-3rd antibacterial classes)

| Class (ATC) | Exposures | Patients | 7-day tx-change rate* |
|---|---|---|---|
| Other β-lactams — cephalosporins/carbapenems (J01D) | 3.23M | 363K | 19.1% |
| Other antibacterials — glycopeptides, metronidazole, etc. (J01X) | 1.48M | 152K | **48.5%** |
| Penicillins incl. β-lactamase combos (J01C) | 1.33M | 179K | 22.7% |
| Quinolones / fluoroquinolones (J01M) | 1.03M | 87K | 21.5% |
| Sulfonamides + trimethoprim (J01E) | 941K | 83K | 19.2% |
| Macrolides/lincosamides (J01F) | 685K | 97K | 20.0% |
| Tetracyclines (J01A) | 501K | 81K | 17.4% |
| Aminoglycosides (J01G) | 165K | 39K | **55.2%** |

*Rate = share of patients whose first exposure to that class is followed within 7 days by a start of a *different* antimicrobial class (a coded switch/escalation proxy).

## Direct answer

- **Most prescribed among the high-resistance-signal classes:** cephalosporins/carbapenems (J01D, 3.2M exposures) lead by a wide margin, followed by penicillins (J01C) and fluoroquinolones (J01M). These three are also the classes most often flagged for resistance in AMR surveillance.
- **7-day treatment change is common but class-dependent:** the "workhorse" high-volume classes cluster around **19–23%** (cephalosporins 19.1%, penicillins 22.7%, fluoroquinolones 21.5%). The strikingly high switch rates are in **aminoglycosides (55%)** and **other antibacterials/glycopeptides (48%)** — expected, since those are typically used as short adjuncts alongside a β-lactam backbone rather than standalone courses.

## Caveats
- "Treatment change" here is a **class-switch proxy** from `drug_exposure` timing, not an explicitly coded stop/change reason (OMOP has no native "changed due to resistance" flag). It counts any different-class start within 7 days, which includes planned combination therapy, IV→PO transitions, and de-escalation — not only failures.
- Classes were grouped at ATC 3rd level; carbapenems and 3rd-gen cephalosporins sit inside J01D and glycopeptides inside J01X, so those specific high-resistance agents aren't broken out above. I can drill into ATC-4th (e.g. carbapenems J01DD/J01DH, glycopeptides J01XA) if useful.
